docs.text: The Lake Erie lake effect snow machine is running at full throttle. Things really cranked up here in Lake County Ohio this morning at about 9:45 and it’s been whiteout conditions since then. Here’s a look out my back door, it looks like heavy fog and visibility just feet away is horrible!

10 years ago today, we braced for a firehose of snow off of Lake Erie for one of the largest snowfall events in Buffalo history (5 FEET of snow). Here are all the low level scans from KBUF. The variable speed of the movie changes because of the scan pattern of the radar

Incredible Edge of Lake Snow Band! - From 0" to 1-2 Feet in a few miles - Massive 4-day event with 3-4ft totals - Lake Erie fell from 50F to 45F during the storm Lake Erie served up a "Thanksgiving Weekend Snow Feast" firing up a band of lake snow.

The nice thing about this past week of chilly is that Lake Erie is now ~80% iced over, so lake effect snow is mostly out of the picture for us. More importantly, there’s now erosion protection of the shorelines in place from the ice. Most importantly, it’s easier for northern birds to cross!😁

November 17-19, 2014: A massive lake effect snow event impacted Buffalo, New York. Over the course of 3 days, bands from Lake Erie produced snowfall rates up to 3-6" per hour. Totals in many areas peaked at over five feet. Tragically, thirteen people were killed.

November 19, 2014:
A massive lake effect snow event finally ended in the Buffalo, NY, metro. From the 17th to the 19th, bands from Lake Erie produced snowfall rates up to 3-6" per hour. Totals in many areas peaked at over five feet. Sadly, 13 fatalities occurred.
